newsitem.title: USA: Northeast submits employee concerns plan.
newsitem.headline: Northeast submits employee concerns plan.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Monday it has submitted a plan to federal regulators on how the company will review and tackle safety issues raised by employees.
The plan was prepared after the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) last October ordered Northeast to address safety issues raised by employees, Northeast said in a statement.
The NRC also told Northeast not to discriminate against employees for raising safety concerns.
Northeast's three Millstone nuclear power plants in Waterford, Conn., have been closed for safety reasons since March of last year.
The three plants had a combined capacity of 2,700 megawatts.
Northeast has said it plans to have all three units ready to be restarted by early 1998.
The company said its new employee concerns plan was the result of two months' work by a volunteer task force.
"The task force effort was extensive," Northeast Nuclear President and Chief Executive Bruce Kenyon said in a statement.
"Their ideas and concepts are now the foundation of our campaign to put these issues behind us. I am committed to this program because it will work to the employees' benefit."
The safety concerns process under the new guidelines will be more "user friendly," Northeast said.
It includes ways to track progress and effectiveness in meeting employees' expectations in how their concerns are addressed.
